set.hook: The two-star Jeunet table at Germigney is gone; the château now feeds guests at La Table du Château.
set.why: Maison Jeunet moved from Arbois to the Château de Germigney at Port-Lesney on 12 November 2021 and kept its two stars in March 2022. Steven Naessens then left in July 2023 (Pudlowski). The room became Maison Rosella under Francesco Di Marzio, starred in March 2024, and since 21 September 2026 the château's kitchen belongs to Alexandre Marza, 28, a Jura-born cook who trained at Maison Jeunet in Arbois and returns with a menu built on Jura producers.
set.verdict: Do not send guests here for Naessens or for the two stars: both are history, and the Jura tourist board's March 2026 count of starred tables names only three, none of them at Germigney. The château itself trades, and Marza's La Table du Château is new enough that no guide has rated it yet. Worth a look as a grand-night option once someone has eaten there.
set.signature: None now: the Naessens menu ended in 2023. At the successor table, the four-course menu (135 euros).
set.caveat: Under the old name this table no longer exists; the successor serves dinner Wed-Sun and lunch Fri-Sun only, 30 km north of Lons

set.hook: Pupillin's village auberge, starred in March 2026, cooking snails, trout and Bresse hen with Jura wine.
set.why: Vivien Sonzogni and Noémie Paris took over the Grapiot in 2024 with partners who mostly met at catering school in Poligny, helped by a Gault&Millau young-talent grant. Two years later came the first MICHELIN star, the Jura's third. The kitchen works with Morteau, cancoillotte, Planches trout and Bresse poultry; the cellar is almost all Jura, and the wine bar on the lower terrace won a Cep d'Or 2025 for its Poulsard service. Pierre Overnoy's domaine is a few doors away.
set.verdict: The most exciting table on the slope this year, and still priced like a village restaurant: 60 euros buys the starred kitchen. Gault&Millau 2026 gives 14.5/20 and calls the Bresse hen with morels exemplary. Hours differ between listings, so call before driving, and pair lunch here with a Pupillin cellar visit rather than making it a late dinner run from Lons.

set.caveat: Closed Monday; Sunday dinner and weekday hours disputed between listings; book by phone; about 30 km from Lons

set.hook: Arbois Bib Gourmand by the Cuisance, run by two Jeunet-trained cooks, with an all-Jura wine list.
set.why: Jérôme Brousseau cooks and Lisa Vuillemin makes the desserts; both came up through the Jeunet kitchen in Arbois and took this room on the Faramand in 2019. The house plate is a ballottine of Planches trout stuffed with morels and oyster mushrooms in a Vin Jaune sauce, river fish from a few kilometres upstream. MICHELIN made it its Bib of the month in October 2023, and the wine list stays inside the Jura.
set.verdict: The sensible lunch on the slope: the 'Au fil du jour' menu is what MICHELIN calls unbeatable value, and Gault&Millau 2026 rates the kitchen 13/20 and the town's leading table. It is bistro cooking with serious technique, not a tasting-menu event. From November the Thursday dinner goes, so plan Arbois evenings for Tuesday, Wednesday, Friday or Saturday.
set.signature: Planches trout ballottine with morels and oyster mushrooms, Vin Jaune sauce
set.caveat: Closed Sunday and Monday, and Thursday evenings November-March; book lunch; about 40 km from Lons

set.hook: A 32-cover bistro on rue Émile Monot with a short regional menu built for sharing.
set.why: The dining room sits a few steps below the street, small enough that the kitchen is never far. The menu is short, three or four starters and mains, and diners say it changes monthly. Gault&Millau's 2026 reviewer ate a crust of morels in Vin Jaune, fondues, duck with Macvin and a dessert pairing goat's cheese with chocolate, and found a cellar of Jura bottles to match.
set.verdict: The most local cooking inside Lons, at prices that suit a crew lunch, but it is a modest bistro, not a destination: Gault&Millau selects it without a score. The room is tiny and the opening hours are irregular and disputed, so phone the same morning. Order the morel crust and whatever Jura white the cellar suggests.

set.hook: A roadside auberge on the Besançon road keeping the Jura classics, ending on a Macvin soufflé glacé.
set.why: Out on the route de Besançon at the northern edge of Lons, with free parking at the door, this is where the region's classic plates are cooked straight: a crust of morels in Vin Jaune, Jura trout with roasted bacon, and for dessert a soufflé glacé flavoured with Macvin, the Jura's grape-must-and-marc aperitif, or griottine cherries from Fougerolles. Gault&Millau calls it quiet and steady.
set.verdict: A safe traditional dinner close to town, rated 11/20 by Gault&Millau, with the 47 euro Menu des Gourmets as the full tour. Diner reviews are mixed: an August 2026 TripAdvisor review complained of a cool welcome and prices, while others praise the cooking. Go for the classics and the soufflé, not for a polished service.
set.caveat: Hours disputed between listings (Saturday especially); a car or taxi from the centre; reviews mention cool service

set.hook: Half Lyon bouchon, half Jura kitchen, with meat grilled on a wood stove in the middle of the room.
set.why: The menu runs on two tracks: Lyonnais bouchon plates such as tablier de sapeur, breaded and fried tripe, beside Jura recipes such as an oeuf cocotte with Comté and Macvin sauce. The meat is grilled on a wood-burning stove set in the centre of the dining room, so the room smells of the fire. Gault&Millau 2026 calls it Lons's institutional brasserie, where people come for business lunches.
set.verdict: A reliable, generous table rather than a fine one: Gault&Millau's 2026 entry keeps it in the guide with a market menu at 37.95 euros, and recent reviews praise the welcome. Order from the fire or the pike quenelle. Hours vary between listings, but it serves both lunch and dinner on most weekdays, which makes it the easiest booking in town.

set.caveat: Closed Sunday; Monday and Saturday hours disputed between listings; busy with business lunches

set.hook: The table under the arcades of Place de la Comédie, with a weekly market menu and five- and six-course menus.
set.why: La Comédie faces the 1840 theatre on the square where the Thursday and Saturday markets set up, and its menus follow them: a market menu that changes each week, a seafood menu, and two longer runs, the five-course Plaisir and the six-course Découverte. One of its former cooks, Alexandre Marza, now runs the kitchen at the Château de Germigney.
set.verdict: A useful market-day lunch in the centre with a choice of menu lengths, but it is not in the Gault&Millau 2026 Lons selection and no 2026 press review was found, so it rests on directory listings and diner reviews. Keep it as the fallback if a kept Lons table is full; check prices when booking.

set.hook: Stone-and-beam bistro on Place Perraud doing andouillette, tête de veau and guinea fowl at low prices.
set.why: The square takes its name from Jean-Joseph Perraud, the Jura-born sculptor, and the restaurant sits in a renovated room of bare stone and exposed beams. Gabriel Janod cooks the French bistro canon: a cassolette of andouillette in mustard cream, tête de veau with gribiche sauce, supreme of guinea fowl. Gault&Millau calls it a reliable address that regulars and visitors both like.
set.verdict: Cheap and dependable, with Gault&Millau's 11/20 and prices around 18-24 euros, which makes it the crew lunch of the Lons tables. It is not where to taste the Jura's freshwater cooking: the pochouse the old guide promised is not on any current menu found. Kept as an alternate; nothing dated 2026 beyond directory updates confirms it.
set.caveat: Closed Sunday and Monday; dinner start time differs between listings; pochouse not confirmed

summit.title: Stars along the wine road
summit.story: The Jura's starred cooking sits on the wine road north of Lons, not in the town. In Pupillin, the Ploussard village, Vivien Sonzogni and his partners took over the Grapiot in 2024 and won its first MICHELIN star in March 2026, the department's third; Gault&Millau names the Bresse hen with morels its classic. Ten minutes away in Arbois, Jérôme Brousseau and Lisa Vuillemin, both trained at Jeunet, cook Planches trout with morels in Vin Jaune under a Bib Gourmand by the Cuisance. The Jeunet name itself has left the slope: its two-star table at the Château de Germigney in Port-Lesney ended in 2023, and Alexandre Marza has cooked there since September 2026.
summit.where: La Table du Grapiot, Pupillin; Le Bistronôme, Arbois; Château de Germigney, Port-Lesney

lons.title: Lons eats regional
lons.story: Lons has no MICHELIN star or Bib; its own tables are regional bistros that Gault&Millau keeps in its selection. On rue Émile Monot, Ô Tablier seats 32 below street level and serves a short menu of morel crust in Vin Jaune, fondue and duck with Macvin. On rue de Vallière, Le Bistrot des Marronniers divides its menu between Lyon bouchon plates such as tablier de sapeur and Jura ones, grilling meat on a wood stove in the middle of the room. Out on the route de Besançon, La Petite Auberge (11/20) holds to Jura trout with bacon and a soufflé glacé flavoured with Macvin.
lons.where: Ô Tablier, Rue Émile Monot; Le Bistrot des Marronniers, Rue de Vallière; La Petite Auberge, Route de Besançon

_notes: All 8 venues checked from WebSearch extracts only (about 30 searches, no page reads). Status: 5 confirmed (La Table du Grapiot, Le Bistronôme, Ô Tablier, La Petite Auberge, Le Bistrot des Marronniers), 2 unverified (La Comédie and La Table de Perraud: listed and trading by directories updated in 2026, but no dated 2026 review or press), 1 closed (Maison Jeunet par Steven Naessens). Biggest correction: the old guide's two-star Maison Jeunet at Port-Lesney no longer exists. Naessens left in July 2023 (Pudlowski); the room became Maison Rosella par Francesco Di Marzio (one star March 2024); the CDT Jura's March 2026 release counts only three starred Jura tables (Grapiot, La Chaumière in Dole, Château du Mont Joly in Sampans); since 21 September 2026 Alexandre Marza runs La Table du Château at Germigney (dinner Wed-Sun, lunch Fri-Sun, menus 80/135/170-175 euros). The summit lane therefore has only two live kept venues; the editor may want La Chaumière or Mont Joly (not checked here) or La Table du Château (unrated, new) as the third. MICHELIN France 2026 is used through the Jura Tourisme/CDT Jura releases and live MICHELIN pages; no full 2026 Bib list seen, Le Bistronôme's Bib rests on its MICHELIN page. Gault&Millau's Lons page lists five restaurants: Jem, La Petite Auberge, La Table de Perraud, Le Bistrot des Marronniers, Ô Tablier; La Comédie is not among them, contrary to the old guide. Old chef names not found in 2026 sources and omitted: Louise Crétin/Thomas Berthod (Ô Tablier), Véronique and Nicolas Narbey (La Petite Auberge, named only by an undated source), Lucie and Guillaume Ferrier (La Comédie), David and Jean-Michel (Marronniers). Bistronôme pastry chef is Lisa (not Léa) Vuillemin. No venue published an annual, Toussaint or Christmas closure; all are open in late October on their regular days. From November Le Bistronôme drops Thursday dinner. Hours disputes left as 'Call ahead' for Grapiot, Ô Tablier, Petite Auberge and Marronniers. No address moved street, so no lat/lng drops (Grapiot is now 3 rue Bagier, same street); Maison Jeunet has no coordinates. Fromagerie Vagne is not in this input file and was not checked here.
